events.speaker: user
events.text: Hi, uh, is this Marisa Kettering? This is Claire Donovan, from The Herakles.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Yep, that's me. Hi, Claire.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Hi! Just so you know, I've got an assistant running that analyses the call. It helps me with my notes. Is that okay with you?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Oh, sure, that's fine.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Thanks. So, we're a digital studio. I was looking at contractor sites around here and, um, yours came up. I'm curious. How do most of your new clients find you these days?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Hm. Honestly? Mostly word of mouth. Referrals. Some from the website, I guess, but... yeah. Mostly referrals.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Mm-hmm. And when someone does land on your site, what do you want them to do?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Well, call us, ideally. But, uh, look, my nephew actually built our site. He kind of looks after it, so we're, we're covered there.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Oh, that's great, family helping out. Does he, um, update it much? Like, with your new projects?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Ha. No. Not really. The last project on there is, gosh, the Halvorsen kitchen. That was, what, four years ago?

events.speaker: user
events.text: Right. And that's, that's something we hear a lot. Contractors do beautiful work, but the site doesn't show it. So we build sites where you snap a photo on the job, and it's in your portfolio in, like, two minutes. Plus a quote request form that sorts leads by job size.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Oh, huh. By job size? That'd, that'd actually help. We get a lot of, um, can-you-fix-my-fence calls.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Exactly. You'd see the big jobs first. And your nephew can stay in the loop if he wants.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Mm. Okay, but honestly, I'm on site six days a week. I just don't have the, the bandwidth to babysit a big project right now.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Totally fair. It's about three hours of your time, total. We do the photos, we do the writing. You just tell us yes or no.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Three hours? Really?

events.speaker: user
events.text: Really. Two short calls and one review.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Okay. And... the cost? Because, uh, we just bought a new excavator, so money's kind of, kind of tight this quarter.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Understood. Projects start around six thousand, and we can split that over six months. And honestly? One extra kitchen job usually pays for the whole thing.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Oh, well, yeah, one kitchen is way more than that. Okay. I'm, I'm actually kind of excited about this!

events.speaker: user
events.text: Wonderful. So how about a thirty-minute call where I show you a couple of contractor sites we've done? Thursday morning, maybe?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Thursday... hmm, mornings I'm on site. Could we do Thursday at, like, four?

events.speaker: user
events.text: Four on Thursday works perfectly.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Great! Oh, and can I bring my nephew? He'll want to see it. He'll probably want to steal ideas, honestly.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Absolutely, bring him. I'll send an invite to the email on your site. Thanks so much, Marisa.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Thank you, Claire! Talk Thursday.
